payload.problem_addressed: Scientific equation discovery (symbolic regression) from finite, noisy data, where numerical fit and syntactic complexity alone are insufficient to establish that a recovered expression is scientifically credible rather than merely a plausible interpolant.
payload.method_summary: AutoSR builds a branching tree of 'Research States' -- each a persistent record of a candidate equation plus its motivation, computational artifacts, and an independent reviewer's diagnosis/score -- via a proposer-reviewer agent cycle. Progressive-widening Monte Carlo tree search (PW-MCTS) with a pending-aware WU-UCT selection rule allocates search effort across branches using percentile-normalized reviewer-score rewards, while a mandatory scientific requirement acts as a hard acceptance gate rather than a tradeable fit criterion; a secondary conventional-SR loop (PySR/SISSO/FEX) feeds the same final synthesis.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper introduces Research-Space Symbolic Regression and formulates Research-State Search as the underlying sequential decision problem, the first such formulation. It implements AutoSR, combining persistent Research States, independent proposer/reviewer roles, and PW-MCTS-based search, and demonstrates exact algebraic recovery on nine selected challenge equations across two benchmark suites, including three cp3-bench problems no prior published system recovered.
key_architecture_choices: Persistent Research State record (candidate equation + motivation + computational artifacts + review + score + parent pointer)
Separate proposer and reviewer agent roles per node, with review as a mandatory acceptance gate for hard scientific requirements
Progressive-widening MCTS (kpw, beta control branching growth) with pending-aware WU-UCT for asynchronous parallel evaluation
Percentile-normalized reviewer score used as the MCTS reward to keep exploration pressure scale-invariant across problems
Branch-local memory: a child inherits its ancestral path's record but not sibling branches, letting alternatives develop independently
Secondary conventional symbolic-regression actor-reviewer loop (PySR, SISSO, FEX) feeding the same final synthesis/report
datasets: cp3-bench (cosmology/astroparticle-physics symbolic regression benchmark, 3 selected unsolved problems)
LSR-Transform subset of LLM-SRBench (6 selected structurally diverse problems)
payload.headline_results: AutoSR recovered algebraically equivalent relations on all 9 selected challenge equations (3 cp3-bench cases that none of 12 published SR baselines recovered, plus 6 LSR-Transform cases), each within roughly 6-33 minutes of proposer time, using the same core search procedure and agent roles throughout.
claimed_advantages: Preserves the full research record (motivation, artifacts, failed tests, review), not just a formula and score, so descendant investigations can build on accumulated evidence
Independent branches let competing explanations develop without premature convergence to one expression
Reviewer enforces mandatory scientific requirements as acceptance conditions rather than trading them off against numerical fit
Produces an auditable final report connecting the leading equation to its evidence, limitations, and credible alternatives
limitations: Evaluated on only 9 selected (not randomly sampled) challenge cases with a single recovered trajectory reported per case -- no benchmark-wide accuracy or repeated-run reliability established
No component ablations isolating the contribution of tree search vs. review vs. branch memory vs. the conventional-SR loop
Cannot rule out memorized scientific knowledge influencing recovery on established public benchmarks
Proposer and reviewer roles may share similar pretrained biases, undermining the independence the review is meant to provide
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The core search architecture -- MCTS with progressive widening over persistent search states, percentile-normalized rewards, and a separate reviewer role that GATES acceptance on hard requirements rather than trading them for fit -- is directly transferable to hexgen's best-of-N + frozen-verifier setup: replace flat best-of-N sampling of full programs with an MCTS over partial hexmesh-DSL programs where the frozen verifier plays the reviewer's role (hard pass/fail on compiles/zero-inverted-elements/etc.) and only requirement-satisfying children are retained/expanded; branch-local memory of failed attempts (with their verifier diagnostics) is also a natural fit for DAgger-style repair distillation.
payload.reviewer_notes: This is a symbolic-regression paper, not CAD/geometry, so the transfer is purely architectural (MCTS + persistent-state + verifier-gated acceptance), not domain-specific. The evaluation is admittedly small-N/cherry-picked and lacks ablations, so the MCTS-over-Research-States idea should be treated as promising but unvalidated at scale -- would want our own ablation of progressive-widening hyperparameters (kpw, beta) before adopting.
dependencies_on_other_methods: Monte Carlo tree search / UCT (Kocsis and Szepesvari)
PySR, SISSO, FEX as the conventional-SR loop's engines

provenance.problem_addressed: Finite data underdetermine the generating function...structurally different expressions can attain nearly indistinguishable errors...while differing sharply in scientific implications
provenance.method_summary: Proposer-reviewer agents develop these states under progressive-widening Monte Carlo tree search (PW-MCTS)
provenance.contributions_summary: we introduce Research-Space Symbolic Regression and, to our knowledge, the first formulation of Research-State Search
provenance.headline_results: AutoSR recovers algebraically equivalent relations in every case, including three cp3-bench problems that no published system recovers
provenance.claimed_advantages: A candidate that violates a requirement identified by the problem specification cannot be presented as an acceptable scientific relation solely because it attains a strong numerical fit.
provenance.limitations: The present evidence is limited to nine selected challenge cases, with one recovered trajectory reported for each.

payload.problem_addressed: Long-horizon embodied household task planning where VLM/LLM-generated plans are fluent but not guaranteed executable, because errors in visual grounding and action-precondition satisfaction compound across an autoregressive rollout.
payload.method_summary: A two-phase neurosymbolic agent: Phase I couples a VLM to a deterministic exploration harness that actively acquires only goal-relevant objects/relations via egocentric observation and grounded interaction, producing a symbolic initial state and object bindings. Phase II plans over this grounded state under a PDDL transition model: at each decoding step the token distribution is masked to only tokens that extend a currently-applicable action (state-dependent constrained decoding), and Monte Carlo tree search (token-level PUCB, combining the constrained LM prior with a domain-independent planning heuristic value) searches over executable continuations, so every returned plan is executable by construction.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper presents a two-phase architecture separating task-directed visual state acquisition from goal-directed symbolic planning through a narrow grounded-state interface. It introduces a state-dependent decoding procedure that enforces PDDL action applicability at the token level, coupled with language-guided MCTS over executable plan prefixes, guaranteeing plans are executable by construction under the transition model. It empirically validates the approach on VirtualHome and ALFWorld against direct visual and embodied-model baselines, with component ablations, cost analysis, and causal failure attribution.
key_architecture_choices: Two-phase POMDP factorization: exploration (state acquisition) then classical planning (deliberation) rather than one entangled autoregressive policy
State-dependent constrained decoding: next-token distribution masked to only tokens extending PDDL-applicable actions, recomputed after every action boundary as the symbolic state advances
Token-level MCTS using PUCB (policy-prior upper confidence bound) that combines the constrained LM prior with backed-up search value
Plan evaluation via a domain-independent planning heuristic (weighted Fast Forward / LM-cut / remaining-plan-cost) rather than a learned critic
Grounded initial-state interface: only the final fact set and symbol-to-instance binding cross from Phase I into Phase II, no raw visual input reaches the planner
datasets: VirtualHome (200 unique problems, 4 goal families, Unity apartments)
ALFWorld (134 unseen-split episodes, 6 task families, AI2-THOR)
metrics: failure attribution by causal stage (exploration/representation vs. grounding/semantics vs. goal-not-reached)
payload.headline_results: Open Qwen3.5 models (4B-27B) reach 94.5-99.5% success in VirtualHome and 90.3-97.8% in ALFWorld; the 4B agent beats a 27B direct-visual-policy baseline by 32.0 and 63.4 points respectively. Constraints and MCTS search are complementary: in ALFWorld, constraints alone or MCTS alone each solve under a third of tasks, but combined they solve over 95%. The method uses up to 4.0x fewer generated tokens than extended thinking and up to 5.6x fewer model-visible images than direct interaction; residual failures concentrate almost entirely in Phase-I state acquisition (2.3-4.5% of tasks) rather than in plan generation.
claimed_advantages: Every returned plan is applicable/executable under the transition model by construction (formal validity guarantee via induction on the PDDL applicability mask)
Substitutes explicit symbolic structure for model scale: a much smaller model with the pipeline beats a much larger direct-policy model
Lower inference and environment-observation cost than unconstrained search or free-form reasoning at matched model scale
Localizes residual uncertainty to the visual state-acquisition stage rather than letting perceptual, grounding, and planning errors compound
limitations: The executability guarantee transfers to the real environment only if the PDDL domain model is sound and Phase I's object-instance binding is correct -- it cannot recover an object Phase I fails to perceive
Not a general hallucination detector: visual recognition errors (e.g. small, low-contrast objects) still cause Phase I failures that propagate to planning
Restricted to discrete, semantically meaningful action planning, not continuous control or motion generation
Phase II never receives environment feedback (open-loop plan), unlike direct-policy and visual-interaction baselines which get feedback every step
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The state-dependent constrained decoding + MCTS-over-executable-prefixes pattern is close to directly transferable to hexgen: mask the decoder's token distribution at each step to only tokens/pointer targets that keep the partial hex-meshing program compileable/executable under the deterministic mesher's grammar (analogous to PDDL applicability), then use token/step-level MCTS with PUCB (LM prior + a value from partial verifier checks, e.g. partial Jacobian/element-budget feasibility) to search over executable program prefixes rather than relying on flat best-of-N sampling after the fact. Their component ablation (Table 2, constraints-alone vs. search-alone vs. combined) is a template for validating whether constrained decoding or MCTS (or both) is where hexgen's structural-validity gains actually come from.
payload.reviewer_notes: Domain is household robot planning (PDDL/VirtualHome/ALFWorld), not CAD, so transfer is purely at the decoding/search-architecture level. Note the validity guarantee is conditional on domain-model soundness and correct instance grounding -- for hexgen the analogous caveat is that constrained decoding only guarantees syntactic/grammar validity, not full verifier pass (quality bounds, surface-match fidelity still need best-of-N/MCTS value guidance as this paper does with its planning heuristic). Ablation Table 2 is worth replicating in miniature for hexgen before committing engineering effort.
dependencies_on_other_methods: PDDL formalism and Fast Downward heuristics (Fast Forward, LM-cut, remaining plan cost)
PUCB / prior-weighted UCT (Silver et al., AlphaGo Zero-style)
SEM-CTRL semantically controlled decoding (prior work by overlapping authors) as closest related constrained-decoding-plus-search method

provenance.problem_addressed: Language and vision-language models generate plausible embodied plans but do not guarantee executability, as their outputs can violate environment dynamics or act on incorrectly grounded entities.
provenance.method_summary: a PDDL transition model restricts decoding to tokens that extend applicable actions. Monte Carlo tree search then evaluates executable continuations using a domain-independent planning heuristic.
provenance.contributions_summary: a state-dependent decoding procedure that enforces PDDL action applicability at token level, coupled with language-guided MCTS over executable plan prefixes, so that plans are executable by construction
provenance.headline_results: open 4B-27B models exceed 90% success in both environments...in ALFWorld either alone solves under a third of tasks, whereas their combination solves over 95%
provenance.claimed_advantages: The resulting plans are executable by construction under the transition model, with transfer to the environment conditioned on correct visual grounding.
provenance.limitations: formal constraints cannot recover an object that Phase I fails to perceive.

payload.problem_addressed: Ensuring correctness of LLM-generated code on complex, repository-level tasks, where prior approaches treat self-generated tests as static post-hoc validators that can be biased/incomplete and cannot guide implementation before code is written.
payload.method_summary: TDD-Agent is a single agent operationalizing test-driven development: Phase 1 (test-first specification) has the agent inspect the repository and write an initial executable test suite before any implementation, forcing it to disambiguate requirements. Phase 2 (dual-track co-refinement) iteratively generates/executes the implementation against the current tests and, on both success and failure, lets the agent revise BOTH the code and the tests (not just the code) based on execution feedback, for up to 10 rounds or until it invokes an early-termination tool.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper proposes TDD-Agent, which adapts test-driven development to LLM code generation by treating test generation as a reasoning step performed before implementation rather than a fixed post-hoc validator. It shows on LiveCodeBench (via a lightweight TDD-prompt variant) that test-first reasoning alone consistently improves over CoT/SCoT/Self-Planning/ICoT baselines. On the repository-level RepoEval benchmark, the full TDD-Agent framework, which additionally allows tests themselves to be revised jointly with code across iterations, consistently outperforms retrieval-based (RAG, RepoCoder) and agent-based (mini-SWE-agent) baselines.
key_architecture_choices: Single agent with persistent conversation history, autonomous over both code and test edits (vs. multi-agent programmer/tester split)
Two-phase workflow: test-first specification setup, then an iterative dual-track test-code refinement loop driven purely by execution feedback (no external oracle)
Dual-track refinement: unlike prior work that freezes tests as immutable constraints, both code and the generated test suite are revisable each iteration

Lightweight tool box: Directory Viewer, Structure Inspector, File Reader, Code Searcher (grep/find) for context; Artifact Submission + pytest-based Test Runner for execution; Early Terminator to stop when the agent judges the task complete
Bounded iteration budget (max 10 rounds) with early termination as the stopping rule instead of a fixed single-shot generation
datasets: RepoEval function-completion subset: 455 problems across 8 Python repositories
metrics: execution-based Pass rate against repository's own held-out unit tests (RepoEval)
average prompt/completion token usage and LLM call count
generated-test pass rate / line coverage rate / mutation score (MutPy) against the ground-truth implementation
payload.headline_results: On LiveCodeBench, TDD-prompt reaches 70.04/67.86/44.87% pass@1 on GPT/DeepSeek/Qwen, best among all prompting baselines tested. On RepoEval, TDD-Agent-iter10 reaches 78.24/90.77/59.34% pass rate on GPT/DeepSeek/Qwen, beating mini-SWE-agent (61.31/84.18/52.97%), RepoCoder, RAG, and In-File baselines; TDD-Agent already surpasses mini-SWE-agent by its 5th iteration at comparable token cost. Ablation shows both test-first generation and dual-track (test+code) refinement are each necessary: single-track (tests frozen after first generation) and reflect-only (no test generation) variants underperform the full method.
claimed_advantages: Test-first generation surfaces the model's assumptions about inputs/outputs/edge cases before implementation, functioning as an executable intermediate representation of task intent
Dual-track refinement lets the agent correct flawed or incomplete self-generated tests, not just implementation bugs, improving downstream feedback quality over iterations
Comparable token/LLM-call cost to a general software-engineering agent (mini-SWE-agent) at 5 iterations while achieving higher pass rates
Iterative refinement measurably improves test quality itself (pass rate, coverage, mutation score against ground truth), not only code correctness
limitations: Credit-assignment risk: the agent can fix correct code to satisfy a hallucinated test, or discard a valid test to accommodate buggy code (observed in <10% of failed cases)

Dominant failure mode is 'matched failure': implementation passes its own generated tests but fails the held-out repository oracle -- the generated tests are an internally consistent but incomplete specification, so defects unexercised by them stay invisible through refinement
Evaluation confined to Python; lightweight tool set gives limited semantic repository understanding (no call-graph/dependency-aware navigation)
Assumes execution feedback is reliable; flaky/nondeterministic tests could mislead the refinement loop (not empirically evaluated)
Iterative nature inherently costs more tokens/latency than single-shot generation
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The dual-track refinement loop -- iteratively revising BOTH the generated artifact and its own self-check (here: tests; for hexgen: candidate program) using execution/verifier feedback, rather than treating the verifier as a fixed post-hoc filter -- is a directly transferable pattern for repair/edit distillation (care area 1): after a best-of-N candidate program fails the frozen verifier, feed the specific verifier failure signal (e.g. which check failed: compiles / inverted elements / Jacobian bound / surface fidelity) back to the model for targeted repair, and track iteration-level improvement the way this paper tracks pass-rate-per-iteration, rather than only doing flat resampling.
payload.reviewer_notes: Domain is software/code generation, not geometry, and the 'test' side of the dual-track loop has no clean hexgen analogue (our verifier is frozen and machine-checkable, not something the model generates and can revise) -- so only the code-repair-via-execution-feedback half transfers directly, not the co-evolving-oracle half. Also worth noting: the paper's own failure analysis (matched failures = self-consistent but wrong) is a caution against letting a model-generated proxy substitute for the real frozen verifier, which reinforces hexgen's existing design of keeping the verifier frozen and external.
dependencies_on_other_methods: Baseline comparisons: RepoCoder, mini-SWE-agent, CoT/SCoT/Self-Planning/ICoT prompting

provenance.problem_addressed: Existing approaches often use generated tests as static post-hoc validators, which limits their ability to guide implementation and may introduce misleading feedback
provenance.method_summary: TDD-Agent first prompts the model to generate executable tests...and then performs iterative dual-track refinement over both the generated code and tests using execution feedback.
provenance.contributions_summary: We propose TDD-Agent, which adapts the test-driven development paradigm for code generation.
provenance.headline_results: TDD-Agent already surpasses the mini-SWE-agent baseline by its fifth iteration, and increasing the number of iterations yields further performance gains.
provenance.claimed_advantages: generated tests are most effective when they are treated not as fixed validators but as evolving reasoning artifacts
provenance.limitations: most failures are matched failures, where the generated implementation passes the generated tests but fails the held-out repository tests

payload.problem_addressed: Direct synthesis of high-fidelity, structurally valid B-Rep CAD models, where prior deep generative methods suffer from 'representation brittleness' (padding noise and cross-primitive feature contamination in the latent space) and 'generation brittleness' (error-propagating cascaded/sequential geometry-then-topology generation plus a train-inference mismatch from non-differentiable, post-hoc validity enforcement).
payload.method_summary: HiFi-BRep is a two-stage VAE + latent-diffusion pipeline for B-Rep generation. The topology-aware dual-stream encoder represents each face/edge as a Bezier-parameterized token, restricts all cross-stream (face-edge) attention to topologically adjacent pairs via a hard Topo-Mask, and pools the variable-length token set into a fixed-length latent using learnable queries (eliminating padding). The single-stage validity-constrained decoder predicts face/edge counts first (to build hard padding masks), then jointly decodes geometry and edge-face adjacency in parallel through stacked cross/self-attention blocks, with a row-wise two-peak softmax objective that directly supervises the 'each edge belongs to exactly two faces' manifold constraint as a differentiable training loss. A separate DiT-based latent diffusion model is trained on the resulting clean latent codes for (un)conditional sampling.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper proposes HiFi-BRep, a framework addressing both representation and generation brittleness in B-Rep synthesis. It introduces a compact B-Rep representation (Bezier curves/surfaces plus an explicit edge-face incidence matrix) and a topology-aware encoder that eliminates padding noise via learnable queries and prevents feature contamination via topology-guided (Topo-Mask) attention, yielding a high-fidelity fixed-length latent. It also designs a single-stage decoder that jointly predicts geometry and topology in parallel and enforces the manifold 'two faces per edge' constraint via a differentiable row-wise two-peak objective, rather than deferring validity to post-processing. Experiments show state-of-the-art structural validity and geometric fidelity versus BRepGen, BrepDiff, and DTGBrepGen, plus faster inference.
key_architecture_choices: Dual-stream (face/edge) transformer encoder with a hard Topo-Mask restricting cross-stream attention to topologically adjacent (edge,face) pairs only
Learnable-query pooling of variable-length face/edge token sequences into a fixed-length latent (Lq=48), eliminating padding-induced noise
Single-stage decoder: count-first prediction (face/edge counts) to build hard masks, then parallel joint decoding of geometry and edge-face adjacency (no cascaded/sequential stages)
Row-wise two-peak softmax objective directly supervising the manifold constraint (each edge shared by exactly 2 faces) as a differentiable loss, rather than post-hoc repair
Compact Bezier-curve/surface primitive representation whose endpoints inherently satisfy vertex-connectivity constraints
Downstream DiT-based latent diffusion model trained on the clean VAE latent space for unconditional and conditioned (class/point-cloud/sketch/image) generation
metrics: Compilability (%, exportable as valid STEP via OpenCascade)
Valid (%, watertight + manifold-consistent at kernel level)
reconstruction accuracy (Face/Edge count accuracy, Adjacency accuracy)
payload.headline_results: On DeepCAD, HiFi-BRep attains the highest Validity (72.20%) and lowest MMD-CD (1.05) among compared methods, with a markedly smaller Compilability-Validity gap than the strongest baseline (18.18 vs. 49.28 points for DTGBrepGen). On ABC it achieves the highest Validity (32.66%) with a 2.95-point gap vs. DTGBrepGen's 25.67-point gap. It is also the fastest at inference: 3.83 s/shape vs. 8.09 (BRepGen), 23.55 (DTGBrepGen), and 26.28 (BrepDiff) s/shape -- 2.1x-6.9x faster. Ablations show removing one-stage joint decoding (reverting to cascaded geometry-then-topology) causes the largest drop, Valid 95.2%->69.3% and Adjacency accuracy 97.5%->73.2%.
claimed_advantages: Embedding manifold/topology validity as a differentiable training objective (row-wise two-peak loss) closes the train-inference validity mismatch that post-hoc-repair methods suffer from
Joint single-stage geometry+topology decoding enables bidirectional optimization and avoids irreversible early decisions of cascaded pipelines
Learnable-query pooling and topology-masked attention remove padding noise and cross-primitive feature contamination that destabilize prior encoders
Smaller Compilability-Validity gap than baselines, i.e. compilable outputs are much more likely to also be fully valid (watertight/manifold), not just file-constructible
Faster end-to-end inference than all compared baselines despite the added validity machinery
Code and pretrained models publicly released
limitations: On ABC, HiFi-BRep trails DTGBrepGen on distributional-alignment metrics (COV, MMD-CD, JSD) even though it wins on Validity -- there is a fidelity/validity tradeoff, not a strict dominance
Validity remains only 72.20% (DeepCAD) / 32.66% (ABC) in absolute terms -- most generated shapes are still not fully valid
Ablation isolates architecture components but is run only on DeepCAD reconstruction, not on full unconditional generation quality

Not extracted from provided text: any explicit discussion of scalability limits or failure modes beyond the qualitative artifacts shown in Fig. 4 (rare failure noted but not characterized in the excerpted chunks)
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: Highly applicable to hexgen's B-rep encoder and structural-validity goals: (1) the Topo-Mask idea -- restricting cross-entity attention to only topologically adjacent face/edge pairs via a hard attention mask -- is directly transferable to hexgen's graph-transformer encoder over the B-rep face-adjacency graph, potentially sharpening pointer/copy-head addressing by preventing irrelevant cross-face attention; (2) the row-wise two-peak differentiable-validity-objective pattern (turning a hard combinatorial validity rule -- 'each edge has exactly 2 faces' -- into a supervised, differentiable training signal rather than a post-hoc filter) is a template for embedding some of hexgen's own frozen-verifier checks (e.g. simpler structural ones like feature-edge capture or element-budget sanity) directly into training rather than relying solely on best-of-N + reject; (3) their single-stage parallel joint geometry+topology decoding vs. cascaded generation ablation (Valid 95.2%->69.3% when reverting to cascaded) is direct evidence that jointly generating structure and parameters (as hexgen's pointer/coordinate-vocabulary decoder already does) outperforms sequential decomposition, reinforcing hexgen's existing single-decoder design choice.
payload.reviewer_notes: This is the closest paper of the four to hexgen's actual domain (CAD B-Rep generation) and the highest-confidence match. Code and pretrained models are public (github.com/1nnoh/HiFi-BRep), so architectural details (Topo-Mask implementation, row-wise two-peak loss) could be inspected directly rather than re-derived from the paper text. Note their B-reps are unconditional/class-conditional generative targets (~6-29 faces, similar scale to hexgen's 7-15 faces) rather than a program/DSL output, so this bears on the ENCODER and validity-loss side of hexgen, not the decoder's program-generation grammar.
dependencies_on_other_methods: Latent diffusion / DDPM with a DiT denoiser (Rombach et al.)
DINOv2 (image conditioning) and PointNet++ (point-cloud conditioning) as auxiliary encoders
OpenCascade STEP export/validity kernel for evaluation
Compared against BRepGen, BrepDiff, DTGBrepGen as baselines

provenance.problem_addressed: Existing deep generative methods suffer from two forms of brittleness: representation brittleness...and generation brittleness, stemming from sequential error propagation and a train-inference mismatch due to non-differentiable validity enforcement.
provenance.method_summary: a single-stage decoder jointly predicts geometry and topology in parallel, embedding core manifold constraints as a differentiable learning objective
provenance.contributions_summary: We design a single-stage validity-constrained decoder that jointly predicts geometry and topology in parallel, enforcing manifold constraints via a row-wise two-peak objective
provenance.headline_results: HiFi-BRep attains the highest Validity (72.20%) and the lowest MMD-CD (1.05)
provenance.claimed_advantages: HiFi-BRep exhibits a markedly smaller Compilability-Validity gap than the strongest baseline
provenance.limitations: DTGBrepGen achieves the best distributional alignment (highest COV and lowest MMD-CD/JSD)

payload.impact_rationale: MCTS-over-persistent-verifier-gated-states is a promising architectural template for hexgen's structural-validity search, but it's demonstrated only on symbolic regression with a small, cherry-picked evaluation and no ablations isolating what drives its gains, so expected impact on hexgen is moderate and speculative until validated in our domain.
payload.effort_rationale: Adopting the pattern means building a persistent-state MCTS controller (progressive widening, WU-UCT, percentile rewards) around the existing best-of-N + frozen-verifier loop and re-architecting search over partial programs rather than full ones -- a substantial engineering lift (L, ~8/10), not a drop-in change.

payload.impact_rationale: This is a validated (ablation-backed, two-benchmark) architecture for exactly hexgen's top-priority problem -- guaranteeing structural validity of autoregressively generated programs via constrained decoding + MCTS over executable prefixes -- so a successful port could directly and substantially raise hexgen's best-of-N pass rate and reduce reliance on post-hoc verifier rejection.
payload.effort_rationale: Requires building a grammar/state mask over the hex-meshing DSL analogous to their PDDL-applicability mask, plus a token-level MCTS with a PUCB combining LM prior and partial-verifier-derived value -- moderate effort (M, ~5/10) since hexgen already has a frozen verifier that could supply (or approximate) the search value signal.

payload.impact_rationale: The execution-feedback dual-track refinement loop is a solid template for repair/edit distillation on failed best-of-N candidates, but only half of the pattern (code-side repair) maps to hexgen since our verifier is frozen and external rather than model-generated and revisable, capping the expected impact at moderate.
payload.effort_rationale: Low engineering lift (S, ~3/10): wrapping the existing verifier's structured failure output as feedback into an iterative repair prompt loop is a relatively small addition on top of the current best-of-N + verifier pipeline, reusing infrastructure that already exists.

payload.impact_rationale: Same domain as hexgen (B-Rep CAD generation, similar 6-29 vs. our 7-15 face scale) with a validated, code-released architecture whose ablation directly demonstrates that embedding manifold-validity constraints as a differentiable loss (vs. post-hoc repair) and topology-masked attention meaningfully raise structural validity -- high expected impact given the domain match.
payload.effort_rationale: Topo-Mask attention and a row-wise validity-supervision loss are moderate additions (M, ~5-6/10) to hexgen's existing graph-transformer encoder/decoder -- conceptually compatible with the current architecture, requiring loss-function and attention-mask changes rather than a redesign, though tuning against hexgen's own verifier definitions will take iteration.
